interactions.effect: Risk of lactic acidosis and acute kidney injury. Stop metformin 48h before contrast administration.
interactions.action: HOLD metformin before imaging. Monitor renal function.

interactions.effect: Significantly increased bleeding risk. Potentiation of anticoagulant effect.
interactions.action: Avoid combination unless explicitly instructed by cardiologist. Monitor INR closely.

interactions.effect: NSAIDs reduce methotrexate clearance, causing toxic accumulation.
interactions.action: Avoid NSAIDs in patients on methotrexate. Use paracetamol instead.

interactions.effect: Amiodarone increases digoxin plasma levels by 70-100%, risking toxicity.
interactions.action: Reduce digoxin dose by 50% when starting amiodarone. Monitor ECG and digoxin levels.

interactions.effect: Omeprazole inhibits CYP2C19, reducing clopidogrel antiplatelet effect.
interactions.action: Prefer pantoprazole or ranitidine over omeprazole in patients on clopidogrel.

interactions.effect: Antacids (calcium, magnesium, aluminium) chelate ciprofloxacin, reducing absorption by up to 90%.
interactions.action: Administer ciprofloxacin 2 hours before or 6 hours after antacids.

interactions.effect: Fluconazole inhibits phenytoin metabolism, causing toxic phenytoin levels.
interactions.action: Monitor phenytoin levels closely if combination unavoidable. Reduce phenytoin dose.

interactions.effect: NSAIDs reduce renal lithium clearance, leading to lithium toxicity.
interactions.action: Avoid NSAIDs in patients on lithium. Use paracetamol. Monitor lithium levels.

interactions.effect: Risk of serotonin syndrome — agitation, hyperthermia, tachycardia, seizures.
interactions.action: Avoid combination. If needed, use lowest tramadol dose with close monitoring.

interactions.effect: Rifampicin induces CYP3A4, drastically reducing contraceptive pill efficacy.
interactions.action: Advise additional contraception barrier method throughout TB treatment and 4 weeks after.

interactions.effect: Rifampicin induces warfarin metabolism, markedly reducing anticoagulant effect.
interactions.action: Increase warfarin dose and monitor INR frequently when starting or stopping rifampicin.

interactions.effect: Combination causes severe bradycardia, heart block, and hypotension.
interactions.action: Avoid combination. If essential, use under cardiac monitoring only.

interactions.effect: Alcohol potentiates metformin-associated lactic acidosis risk.
interactions.action: Counsel patients on metformin to avoid heavy alcohol use.

interactions.effect: ACE inhibitors increase potassium retention; combination risks hyperkalaemia.
interactions.action: Monitor serum potassium. Avoid routine potassium supplementation with ACE inhibitors.

interactions.effect: Increased risk of tendon rupture, especially Achilles tendon, in elderly patients.
interactions.action: Avoid fluoroquinolones in patients on steroids where alternatives exist. Warn patient.

interactions.effect: Antacids reduce chloroquine absorption significantly.
interactions.action: Separate doses by at least 4 hours.

interactions.effect: Isoniazid inhibits phenytoin metabolism, increasing phenytoin toxicity risk.
interactions.action: Monitor phenytoin levels in TB patients. Reduce phenytoin dose if needed.

interactions.effect: Both are ototoxic and nephrotoxic; combination greatly amplifies risk.
interactions.action: Avoid concurrent use. If essential, use minimum doses and monitor renal function + hearing.

interactions.effect: Fluconazole inhibits glibenclamide metabolism, causing severe hypoglycaemia.
interactions.action: Monitor blood glucose closely. Reduce glibenclamide dose or switch antifungal.

interactions.effect: Chronic alcohol use increases hepatotoxicity risk from paracetamol.
interactions.action: Limit paracetamol to 2g/day in patients with regular alcohol use.

interactions.effect: Iron chelates tetracycline, reducing antibiotic absorption by 50-90%.
interactions.action: Separate doses by at least 3 hours. Take tetracycline first.

interactions.effect: Iron chelates ciprofloxacin, markedly reducing its absorption.
interactions.action: Administer ciprofloxacin 2 hours before iron. Do not take together.

interactions.effect: Ciprofloxacin inhibits theophylline metabolism, causing theophylline toxicity (seizures, arrhythmias).
interactions.action: Reduce theophylline dose by 30-50%. Monitor theophylline levels.

interactions.effect: Erythromycin inhibits carbamazepine metabolism, leading to toxicity (diplopia, ataxia).
interactions.action: Avoid combination. Use azithromycin instead if macrolide needed.

interactions.effect: Risk of serotonin syndrome — potentially fatal.
interactions.action: Absolute contraindication. Never combine.

interactions.effect: Severe, potentially fatal hypotension due to additive vasodilation.
interactions.action: Absolute contraindication. Do not prescribe together under any circumstance.

interactions.effect: Additive hyperkalaemia risk, especially in renal impairment.
interactions.action: Monitor serum potassium and renal function regularly.

interactions.effect: Disulfiram-like reaction — severe flushing, vomiting, tachycardia.
interactions.action: Strict alcohol abstinence during metronidazole course and 48h after last dose.

interactions.effect: Amoxicillin reduces renal methotrexate clearance, increasing toxicity risk.
interactions.action: Monitor for methotrexate toxicity signs — mucositis, cytopaenia.

interactions.effect: Increased neurotoxicity risk; can cause irreversible brain damage at therapeutic levels.
interactions.action: Use lowest effective doses. Monitor for neurotoxicity signs.
